title: The Hungry Portrait
premise: Folklorist Petra Ishikawa has spent seven years in the village of Hollowmere, recording songs the locals refuse to sing twice, and dismissing the noises beneath the moor as geology. When an excavation crew breaks through a door sealed from the inside, something old and hungry steps into the village wearing the faces and voices of the dead, and it remembers every song Petra has ever collected. As the night stretches toward a sunrise that refuses to come, Petra discovers the village's founders invited the thing in deliberately, feeding it memories to keep it asleep, and that the songs were never warnings but lullabies. To save the ragtag found family that has gathered around them, Petra must sing the hunger awake and offer it their own memories as a new bargain — and at dawn, Petra walks out of Hollowmere unable to remember the people who saved them, while those people remember Petra enough to begin teaching them everything again.
about_author: Edmund Underhill is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing oral histories in remote coastal communities before turning to horror. They write in a drafty farmhouse, where they claim the floorboards sing in a key they refuse to name.

chapters.title: The Second Verse
chapters.summary: Petra Ishikawa, POV. Petra records elderly Maren Voss singing a harvest song; Maren stops abruptly at the seventh verse and refuses, hands shaking, to repeat it. That evening Petra's archive of forbidden verses hums faintly on its own. The beat is quiet unease — seven years of rational explanations beginning to fray at the edges.

chapters.title: What the Moor Kept
chapters.summary: Petra and site foreman Dara Okafor, alternating POV. The excavation crew's ground-penetrating radar shows a chamber beneath the barrow; Dara is eager, Petra uneasy about local warnings. They break through a stone door — sealed from the inside. The beat is transgressive curiosity tipping into dread as cold air pours out carrying a familiar melody.

chapters.title: Voices in the Walls
chapters.summary: Petra, POV. That night, villagers begin speaking in the voices of Hollowmere's dead, including Petra's own late mentor, reciting verses Petra recorded years ago. The pub becomes a refuge for a handful of survivors: Dara, Maren, teenage Tam, and innkeeper Bess. The beat is terror and the first fragile bonds of the found family forming under pressure.

chapters.title: The Lullaby Hypothesis
chapters.summary: Maren, POV. Maren confesses the songs were lullabies, not warnings — the founders' bargain fed the thing beneath the moor their memories, and the singing kept it asleep. Breaking the door let it taste fresh memory. The beat is guilt and revelation, as Maren's lifetime of complicity comes undone.

chapters.title: Sunrise, Postponed
chapters.summary: Dara, POV. Dawn fails to arrive; the sky holds a bruised grey. The thing outside grows bolder, wearing the crew members who didn't make it to the pub, pleading to be let in. Dara, who broke the door, spirals toward self-destruction. The beat is guilt curdling into despair, and Petra pulling him back from the threshold.

chapters.title: The Founders' Ledger
chapters.summary: Petra, POV. Searching the church archive, Petra finds the founders' ledger: the original bargain, the names of the invited, and a final page — the ritual of re-invitation, which requires a living singer to offer memories willingly. Tam, reading over their shoulder, realizes what it costs. The beat is hope shadowed by price.

chapters.title: What the Thing Remembers
chapters.summary: The entity, POV (unusual, intimate). Inside its hunger we see the memories it has eaten — centuries of Hollowmere's dead — and its fixation on Petra's recordings, the richest archive it has ever tasted. It begins singing Petra's own voice back at them through the walls. The beat is horrifying intimacy: it doesn't want to kill Petra; it wants to keep them.

chapters.title: The Door Inward
chapters.summary: Bess, POV. The entity breaches the inn by wearing Bess's drowned brother. Bess holds the doorway — literally, body against the frame — long enough for the others to bar the inner room, and is taken. The beat is devastating sacrifice; the found family loses its first member and hardens its resolve.

chapters.title: The Re-Invitation
chapters.summary: Petra, POV. Climax. In the churchyard at false-dawn, Petra sings the full forbidden cycle, every verse the village refused to sing twice, and offers the entity their seven years of collected memory — the archive itself — as a new seal. The entity accepts; the door reseals from the inside; sunrise breaks. The beat is transcendent terror becoming sacrifice.

chapters.title: Learning the Songs Again
chapters.summary: Petra, POV. Weeks later, Petra wakes in Hollowmere with no memory of the village or the people in it — the price of the bargain. But Maren, Dara, and Tam gather round and begin, gently, to tell them everything, starting with a song Maren sings twice without fear. The beat is bittersweet grace: memory lost, family found again from zero.
